points.t: A patient a few days to weeks after minor skin surgery with a question about the wound, stitches, activity or scar.
Healing goes through inflammation, proliferation and remodelling; tension and infection disrupt it; some people form keloids.

Keep dry 24–48 h then wash; sutures out at 5–7 days on the face, 10–14 on the trunk and arms and about 14 on the back and legs (local protocols vary); avoid strenuous activity for 1–2 weeks; flucloxacillin for wound infection (clarithromycin or doxycycline if penicillin-allergic, checking interactions).
Spreading cellulitis, abscess, dehiscence; keloids in people with skin of colour or on the chest, shoulders and earlobes.

points: **Avoid strenuous exercise, heavy lifting, contact sport and swimming for ~1–2 weeks** (until sutures are out and the wound is sound) to prevent **dehiscence and stretched scars**. course teaching said no football for 2 weeks.

**Work:** a construction worker may need **1–2 weeks of modified or light duties**. The fit note (from any eligible healthcare professional, including pharmacists since July 2022) can advise "may be fit for work with adjustments".
Protect the wound from dust and dirt at work (a waterproof dressing).
**Massage** with emollient once healed (from about 2–3 weeks).
**Sun protection (SPF 30+) for at least a year** to avoid pigmentation.

items.t: Spreading redness, fever, pus or increasing pain after surgery: assess for **wound infection or abscess** the same day.

pearls.t: Give written aftercare with a **named contact for bleeding/infection** and the **date for suture removal and results**.
